title: Microbiome random forest predicts TMAO producer phenotype; mouse model finds key microbe
summary: Individual TMAO production after an oral carnitine challenge identified 39 gut operational taxonomic units correlated with productivity, including Emergencia timonensis. A microbiome-based random forest classifier predicted the producer phenotype with an AUROC of 0.81, which held at 0.80 in an external cohort. A humanized gnotobiotic mouse model identified the novel bacterium Ihubacter massiliensis as a key TMA/TMAO producer; the two bacteria together accounted for 43% of high producers with 97% specificity. The bacterial discovery rests on the mouse experiment, not on the classifier.
ai_technology: Random forest classifier on gut microbiome OTUs predicting TMAO producer phenotype

evidence.tested: External cohort AUROC 0.80; humanized gnotobiotic mouse experiments for the novel microbe.
evidence.unknown: Cohort sizes are not stated in the abstract; the mouse model supports the microbe finding, not the classifier; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A random forest predicted the producer phenotype from microbiome composition.
